title: Converge’s BizKarteng Pinoy podcast closes season 1 with clear message: PH MSMEs must embrace technology

blocks.text: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises, or MSMEs, are critical to the Filipino way of life. In fact, they comprise the backbone of the Philippine economy as they make up about 99 percent of all businesses in the country while providing some 60–63 percent of the nation’s total employment and accounting for about 36 percent of the gross domestic product or GDP. Unfortunately, this critical sector is beset with challenges that make it difficult for business owners at this level to stay open, much less thrive. Filipino MSMEs face multiple interconnected challenges, with technology and digitalization representing a major and persistent barrier that limits their productivity, competitiveness, and growth. In this day and age, Filipino MSMEs are no longer just competing with the business next door; they're competing on a global stage—and they need innovation more than ever now. That reality anchors the Season 1 finale of BizKarteng Pinoy Podcast, the flagship business podcast launched in partnership with Converge SME Solutions. This final episode offers up a clear message: adopting the right technology isn't optional for entrepreneurs who want to scale beyond local markets. Instead, it’s a must. A Season Built on Real Stories Since its launch, BizKarteng Pinoy Podcast has focused on real-world Filipino entrepreneurship, featuring the growth journeys, setbacks, and eventual wins of local business owners and industry figures. Guests like Dawn Chang of DC Delights offered a firsthand look at how personal passions can be turned into scalable businesses. Others such as Char Tinio and Ned Adriano tackled the harder side of entrepreneurship, including recovering from failure, rebuilding, and managing the operational and financial pressures that come with running an MSME. Running through nearly every conversation was a common thread: technology adoption and reliable connectivity as tools that let local businesses compete and scale in a modern market—not as add-ons, but as infrastructure for growth. In other words, BizKarteng Pinoy Podcast touched on the real-world applications of technology, digitalization, and connectivity in running a business. Technology as the Path to Global Competitiveness That thread is what Season 1 ultimately argues: MSMEs that treat technology adoption as central to their operations—not peripheral—are the ones positioned to grow beyond the domestic market and hold their own globally. Whether it's the resilience required to survive a business failure, the operational discipline needed to manage finances, or the digital tools required to serve customers and scale, the season consistently points back to the same conclusion: competitiveness today is a function of how well a business leverages technology, not how big it already is. Taken together, Season 1 paints a fuller picture of what it takes to build, maintain, and ultimately scale a Filipino small business today: the personal journeys behind the brands, the resilience required to survive setbacks, and the digital foundation—connectivity, tools, technology adoption—that determines whether a business can scale past its starting point. Season 1 Goes Full Circle Rounding out the season's expert commentary is Dindo Marzan, Senior Vice President and Head of SME Business Group at Converge ICT Solutions Inc. Marzan is known across the industry as "Mr. MSME," and his insights on the broader MSME ecosystem and market challenges in the Philippines lend added weight to the season's closing conversation. Marzan's talking points get specific about what that foundation actually requires. Among them: why internet connectivity should be treated as a business investment rather than a household utility, and what separates residential internet from a connection built for business use. He also underscores why businesses need dedicated, reliable connectivity to keep daily operations running. Put simply this is the kind of connectivity that supports everything from customer service and digital transactions to cloud-based tools and long-term scaling. Just as important, Marzan flags some of the common misconceptions MSMEs fall into when choosing an internet solution, often underinvesting in infrastructure and then struggling to keep pace with demand. In other words, Season 1’s finale delves deep into the backbone of today’s digital era: strong, reliable connectivity. Ready to Level Up? Season 1 leaves Filipino entrepreneurs with a lot to chew on—real stories, hard-won lessons, and a clear reminder that going global starts with getting the fundamentals right at home. If you're building something and wondering what's next, this season's a good place to start.
